A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix F to v3 Section 7.

before.justification: V1 reports original prediction accuracies, component-decoding results, causal tracing, attention knockouts, and attention-head analyses across two models and three datasets.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical analyses and adds prompt-specific accuracies, five-answer experiments, and ten-answer outcomes in Tables 3–4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Token Lens, component decoding, causal tracing, and attention knockout retain their procedures. Applying them to additional prompts and answer steps extends evaluation. The attention-head characterization in v3 Section 7 already appeared in v1 Appendix F.

E1.justification: The Country-Cities, Artist-Songs, and Actor-Movies domains remain unchanged. V3 Appendix F extends the evaluated task requirements from generating three distinct answers to five and ten answers, without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and comparison methods remain unchanged. V3 explicitly names Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, but v1 already links to that checkpoint's model card. The added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 expands from one to three prompt templates per model/dataset, and most analyses now average across templates. Added longer-list experiments introduce five-answer runs with Template 1 and different evaluation cohorts, plus ten-answer testing. Appendix F's captions conflict with its prose about aggregation scope, but the protocol expansion is clear.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends robustness checks through prompt variation and longer answer lists. Appendix F adds Token Lens and knockout analyses of subject, previous-answer, and last-token contributions through steps 4–5, plus ten-answer feasibility results. The attention-head independence analysis is relocated from v1 Appendix F, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. The attention-head classification using means and standard deviations already exists in v1 Appendix F. Averaging across different prompt conditions does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 scores are retained as Template 1 in v3 Table 3. V3 adds other template scores, revised aggregate plots, three-template averages, and longer-list results. Examples include five-answer Actor-Movies counts of 582/7914 for Llama and 422/7914 for Mistral. These substantially expand the evidence; changes to template-averaged scores are not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The task definition, decoding equation, Token Lens equations, and attention-head classification thresholds remain mathematically unchanged. The classification rule moves from Appendix F to Section 7. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the stated empirical scope of the mechanism to multiple prompt templates. The central promote-then-suppress claim, the roles assigned to attention and MLPs, and the Token Lens contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds an evidence boundary: most five-answer settings and all ten-answer settings yield too few fully correct cases for the intended analyses. Existing mechanism interpretations largely remain. The limitations section still claims single-template evaluation, creating an inconsistency with the expanded experiments.

D1.justification: Table 2 documents the additional prompt wordings, and Figures 16–17 newly specify 100 instances per dataset for causal tracing. This disclosure does not establish a change from v1's actual sample count. Hardware, data-preparation descriptions, and code/data access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Voita et al. (2023) when discussing component functions and Saynova et al. (2024) when discussing unreliable factual recall and future work. These are targeted additions; the positioning around one-to-many recall versus prior one-to-one studies remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. The main structural change promotes v1 Appendix F to v3 Section 7, followed by the renumbered conclusion. V3 also adds the longer-answer appendix and makes localized wording, model-name, and cross-reference edits.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the prompt bullets with Table 2, adds Tables 3–4 and twelve five-answer figures (30–41), and moves v1 Figure 29 into the main text as Figure 7. Figure 1 is redrawn, and appendix plots are redistributed with revised captions. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional prompt evaluations and longer-list tests strengthen support for the existing mechanism and reveal limits in obtaining fully correct examples. Table 3 also exposes prompt-dependent accuracy variation while preserving the original scores. The gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: the unchanged single-template limitation contradicts the experiments, and Appendix F's captions disagree with its description of dataset/template aggregation.
